annotations.text:
Scoreboard, with the court plan on the watch's first screen.

One system throughout: Oswald condensed for anything you read at a glance, JetBrains Mono for labels and data, ink on paper for the phone, paper on ink for the watch, and vermilion reserved for exactly two jobs — the serve, and the one action that starts or ends something.

Watch boards are drawn at 2x (396x484 = 198x242 pt). Both fonts carry Cyrillic, so the Russian build has the same voice.
The court is the button. Tap the half that serves and the match starts — no second Start press. The line under it is there for the first match only; it's the one gesture nobody guesses.
The sentence under the rule is the idea worth stealing from Padel Score Tracker: four separate settings, stated once as what the match will actually be. It changes as you change them.
Ours is the inverted half — paper where theirs is ink. No color needed to tell them apart, which is what survives sunlight, and it leaves vermilion free to mean the serve.

The phone is a full second scorer: the same two-zone split, the same inversion, the same serve dot — so the two halves you tap are in the same places on both devices. Undo is a visible button here rather than the watch's long press: on a phone there is room to say it, and no wet-hand problem to design around.

Open question I did not decide: whether a phone match and a watch match can be the same match — picking up on one where you left off on the other — or whether they are simply two ways to start one. That is a data question (rally journal ownership, delivery direction) before it is a design one.
